scope: A dated discovery and compatibility snapshot, not a live version authority. Check each repository and release for newer evidence. The four releases recorded here were read from their GitHub Release pages, including each asset's published SHA-256.

coordination.work_tracking: The existing Linear WuwaTerm project remains authoritative for work tracking.

api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. The v3 contract ships in Web 0.3.0 and Windows 0.5.0, not in Windows 0.4.2 or Web 0.2.0; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

terms_database.note: Build or obtain the terms database separately; it is not included in the products.

telegram_state.chat_settings: Unversioned JSON with public and allowed fields.
telegram_state.note: Follow Telegram's state and recovery instructions when moving or upgrading.

api_device_store.format: SQLite devices table, separate from the terms database
api_device_store.note: The observed implementation does not declare a numbered schema; preserve the device store and its SQLite state.

web_selfhost_admission.note: This stores aggregate admission counters, not manuscripts, and is separate from Core's databases.

products.responsibility: Shared dictionary, translation and review logic, HTTP API, data builder and validation, and common deployment and recovery tools.

previous_release.manifest_note: The release manifest records source_commit, the runtime and builder image digests and the pinned upstream data revision: runtime sha256:da581ce6ebf5ab12143d4344bbbee8962da188b08c91242cf0106d343b2c3060 and builder sha256:d7fb9bb47891a852507206bb6c2bab7349c99a6e9583020b46fdf3d393b62d40, first pushed as sha-d54957c and retagged by promote-images as v0.9.0 and 0.9.
previous_release.note: v0.9.0 judges review terms paragraph by paragraph when the sentence counts differ (matcher label wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v7), adds the orphan area titles and four-tier item base names to the dictionary (reference-only in Chinese text), adds a per-direction thinking setting for translation requests that defaults to the old request, and moves the Web and Windows contract pins to manuscript v3. Kept as history after v0.9.1; the release and its assets are still published. v0.8.7 and earlier remain on the release page.

candidate_source.note: The 0.7.0 source adds contextual term references and deploy/setup.sh. It was merged as 2ebb3259 and published as v0.7.0; the candidate wheel below belongs to an earlier candidate checkout and is not that source. Kept as history after the release.

candidate_wheel.note: A CI artifact of an earlier candidate checkout, recorded before the release; it is not the published 0.7.0 wheel.

products.adoption_note: Core v0.9.1 (c24cb5d) is deployed on the owner VPS since 2026-11-16 by a runtime-only update: release r5 is current, r4 is retained, and wuwaterm-api reports 0.9.1. terms.db is the 0.9.0 database, unchanged (12,089 terms, data pin 9218d612). WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_ZH_EN is not set in .env, so Chinese-to-English translation requests use the new default disabled. The legacy in-Core wuwaterm-bot is stopped (status=created): the r5 update recreated it on the new image without starting it. Core v0.9.0 (d54957c) was deployed earlier the same day by a full update (release r4). Telegram runs as the standalone wuwaterm-telegram container, now 0.3.1 on Core 0.9.1.
products.transition: The observed Core source still contains the legacy Telegram and private Python Web adapters; retirement depends on usable successors.

products.responsibility: Standalone Telegram bot and its installation, operation and state.

release.note: v0.3.1 pins the published Core 0.9.1 wheel (OCI index sha256:fedaf01484b68cd6c19797901f8a63942b8757ce76c6f451198488470ebc8862, manifest sha256:88018781d9f768efa23b60ac4c49ead147b16b5e25adfb30f32eafe9012556af, config sha256:aa58a053ccd40297fcfc8fb95c1dcde2339135b30cca0d87fff373cbe022b3a7). It is a patch release with no Telegram code changes beyond the Core pin (#40): long /tr and /sentence texts keep the source's paragraph layout, Chinese-to-English translation sends thinking disabled by default, and deploy/env.example now sets WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_ZH_EN=disabled (the 0.3.0 file set omit, so an install copied from it kept thinking on). Production was updated.

compatibility.note: core-lock.json pins the published Core v0.9.1 wheel; release-to-release dependency, not a CI artifact.

previous_release.note: v0.3.0 pins the published Core 0.9.0 wheel (OCI index sha256:28ab3af0ff4d8fdf6f7b3cad76812a245a80348b77e9200d248ec96e27e13ca5, manifest sha256:7dee0ea1ee65eeba32673f352a0a533dbb780ec4a49d2224bc3d3f3e2f6eb26c, config sha256:001e9b20203e8db5c6cb8f6739ceca374eb904455e2c6f85d7404ef6cc310430), settles the review dedup boundaries for TTL, repeats, delivery and /review last (#38), and documents the per-direction translation thinking settings in deploy/env.example (#39). products.adoption_note: Standalone Telegram 0.3.1 on Core 0.9.1 runs on the owner VPS as wuwaterm-telegram since 2026-11-16, as a local image built from the release the way 0.3.0 was: the bot runs wuwaterm 0.9.1 and wuwaterm-telegram 0.3.1 and the container has not restarted. The production .env sets none of WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_ZH_EN, WUWATERM_TRANSLATION_THINKING_EN_ZH and WUWATERM_SEMANTIC_REVIEW_THINKING; inside the running container, Core 0.9.1 computes the Chinese-to-English mode from that environment as disabled (request body {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}) and English-to-Chinese as omit.

products.responsibility: Windows desktop client, local manuscript editing, packaging and independent release.

main.status_note: README-only commit (#26, record of 0.5.0 and its assets) on top of the release commit 277551c. ci.yml is skipped by its paths-ignore for docs-only changes, and the Dependency audit run succeeded (run 43847746394). The CI run that passed is on 277551c.

release.note: v0.5.0 reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v3 and adds resumable long-manuscript work (#19-#22, #24, #25): per-segment term results, choices and progress saved in v3 and readable by Web 0.3.x, a Markdown review report export, and segment-list and editor fixes. Windows 0.4.2 and Web 0.2.0 and earlier reject v3 files. It requires HTTP API v1, and manuscript review also needs review-v2.

compatibility.note: The client reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v1, v2 and v3; local manuscript editing works offline, and online features require a configured API and device credential.

products.responsibility: One browser workbench and same-origin backend for public and self-hosted use; Sites is a hosting target.

release.manifest_note: The published manifest records the archive under archive.name and the build prefix under base_path; the launcher, port and responses belong to the bundle (bundle/start.mjs, PORT defaults to 3000). The archives are the root and prefix candidates of workflow runs 43802468211 and 43802472098, promoted without rebuilding; the manifests name Web CI run 43801860994.
release.note: v0.3.1 is a patch release on v0.3.0: the failure advice for a translation that fails no longer points to the review workbench, which only the experimental semantic workbench offers; it says to retry later or to split a long text into shorter parts and translate each in "Sentence translation". The BFF, the /v1 proxy, the manuscript formats, the database schema, dependencies and hosting configuration are unchanged since v0.3.0. v0.3.0 and its assets remain published under previous_release.

previous_release.manifest_note: The published manifest records the archive under archive.name and the build prefix under base_path; the launcher, port and responses belong to the bundle (bundle/start.mjs, PORT defaults to 3000). The archives are the root and prefix candidates of Web CI run 43791077911, promoted without rebuilding.
previous_release.note: v0.3.0 is the first Web release that reads and writes wuwaterm-manuscript-v3, a file format Web 0.2.0 and Windows 0.4.2 reject: resumable long-manuscript review, clearer failures, choices on truncated segments, current exports, report import, and paragraphs kept on whole-text translation. The BFF, the /v1 proxy, the database schema, dependencies and hosting configuration are unchanged since v0.2.0. v0.2.0 and earlier releases and their assets remain on the release page. Kept as history after v0.3.1; the release and its assets are still published.

compatibility.selfhost_requires: A compatible Core API with GET /v1/auth/status and an issued device credential, plus an authenticated HTTPS reverse proxy that sets X-WuwaTerm-Edge.
compatibility.note: The Web BFF validates response shapes strictly; a matching API version alone does not prove compatibility.

ci_pins.note: These repository pins identify the specified contract-test inputs, not a guarantee for arbitrary version pairs. The Web pin is a main commit that carries manuscript v3 and is an ancestor of the Web v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 tags; the Windows pin is a main commit after Windows 0.4.2 that carries manuscript v3 and is an ancestor of the Windows v0.5.0 tag.
